newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba-Bonn Jan-Oct cash deficit jumps(RPT).
newsitem.headline: Buba-Bonn Jan-Oct cash deficit jumps(RPT).

text.p: The German government's cash deficit more than doubled in the first 10 months of this year compared with last year's results, the Bundesbank said in its November report which was released on Tuesday.
From January through October the Bonn government's cash deficit totalled 68.41 billion marks after posting only 26.58 billion in the same time a year earlier.
In October alone the cash deficit ticked up to 14.5 billion marks compared with three billion marks in October 1995, the Bundesbank said.
But the sharp deterioration needs to be seen in context, the Bundesbank said, explaining that special factors last year helped leave the overall cash deficit relatively low.

"Even in light of the strong deterioration, certain shifts need to be taken into consideration," the Bundesbank said, adding "the development of the government's cash position was particularly positive last year".
In October 1995, for example, the government received funds from privatisations which left the deficit at an "unusually low level," the Bundesbank added.
Because of the relatively low comparison levels, the Bundesbank said the cash deficit for the first 10 months will have been exaggerated as compared with that of the entire year 1996.
At the same time the government's net borrowing climbed to nine billion marks in October, the Bundesbank said, calling the number "very high".
In September borrowing developments were mixed, the Bundesbank said noting the federal government's external borrowings stood at 4.5 billion marks.

The total government indebtedness, which includes the federal, state and local governments, however, was reduced by 2.5 billion marks in September largely because certain borrowings were able to be repaid as tax revenue was slightly higher in that month.

During the first nine months of the year the public sector raised its net borrowings to 62 billion marks after 40.8 billion marks during the same time a year ago, the Bundesbank said, adding the increase was largely due to the federal government's increased demand.
